captions.linkedin:
Here's the factor that quietly replaced value in the 2015 Fama-French model. Nobody talks about it, but its t-statistic is 3.4 and it correlates 0.7 with HML.

The signal: companies that grow their assets slowly outperform companies that grow them aggressively.

Not revenue growth. Not earnings growth. Total asset growth, year over year.

Here's the complete logic from JFE 2015. No black box:

🔹 ASSET GROWTH SIGNAL. Change in total assets divided by lagged total assets, split conservative vs aggressive.
🔹 SIZE-NEUTRAL. Sort independently on market cap, then on investment growth.
🔹 FISCAL-YEAR LAG. Two prior fiscal years of total-assets data required for clean computation.
🔹 ANNUAL REBALANCE. June formation, 12-month hold, low-turnover by design.
🔹 ZERO-COST SPREAD. Long conservative-growth firms funded by short aggressive growers.

Fama and French 2015. CMA mean 0.33% per month, t=3.4 across construction variants. US full sample 1963 to 2013. Weaker internationally, Japan insignificant. You verify it.
